openers.prompt_en: A coach asked Arjun to practise bowling daily. Arjun practised for a month, then won a match. His coach showed him the practice chart. Which happened immediately before the match win: daily practice or seeing the chart?
openers.prompt_hi: Coach ne Arjun ko roz bowling practice karne ko kaha. Arjun ne ek mahina practice ki, phir match jeeta. Coach ne use practice chart dikhaya. Match jeetne se turant pehle kya hua: daily practice ya chart dekhna?
hints: Which event comes just before the win?
Follow the order given in the passage.
He practised, then ___, then saw the chart.
Daily practice came before the match win.

openers.prompt_en: Nisha asked for the answers to a science quiz. Her teacher instead gave her practice questions. After Nisha scored well, the teacher smiled. What did the teacher want Nisha to do: guess, copy or learn through practice?
openers.prompt_hi: Nisha ne science quiz ke answers maange. Teacher ne uske badle practice questions diye. Nisha ka score achchha aaya toh teacher muskuraye. Teacher kya chahte the: guess karna, copy karna ya practice se seekhna?
hints: Why give questions instead of answers?
Notice what Nisha did before scoring well.
The teacher wanted her to ___ rather than copy.
Learn through practice; the teacher gave questions, not answers.

harder.prompt_en: A cricket team bought a ‘lucky’ bat but also trained every morning for weeks. They won after improving their fielding. Which detail best supports the message that effort matters more than luck: buying the bat or improving their fielding?
harder.prompt_hi: Cricket team ne ‘lucky’ bat kharida, par kai hafton tak roz subah training bhi ki. Fielding sudharne ke baad team jeeti. Effort luck se zyada zaroori hai—iska behtar saboot kya hai: bat kharidna ya fielding sudharna?
hints: Which detail shows a change caused by effort?
Compare what the team bought with what they worked on.
Their win followed an improvement in ___.
Improving their fielding; it shows the result of training.

harder.prompt_en: Choose the correct pair: ‘The library book is ___ tomorrow. I ___ the debate yesterday.’ Options: due/won, dew/one, due/one.
harder.prompt_hi: Sahi pair chuno: ‘The library book is ___ tomorrow. I ___ the debate yesterday.’ Options hain: due/won, dew/one, due/one.
hints: Which words fit a deadline and a victory?
Sound-alike words can have different meanings.
Book deadline: ___; debate victory: ___.
Due/won; a book is due, and a debate is won.

harder.prompt_en: Complete with the correct past-tense verb and article: ‘As soon as Riya ___ (see) the notice, she joined ___ art club.’
harder.prompt_hi: Sahi past-tense verb aur article se sentence poora karo: ‘As soon as Riya ___ (see) the notice, she joined ___ art club.’
acceptable: As soon as Riya saw the notice, she joined the art club.
hints: What changes when ‘see’ describes a past event?
Use the irregular past form; identify the particular club.
As soon as Riya ___ the notice, she joined ___ art club.
Saw; the. ‘Saw’ is past tense, and ‘the’ identifies the club.

openers.prompt_en: For a school assembly, two lines end with “light” and “bright”. To make an AABB rhyme pattern, should the next two lines end with “day” and “play”, or “night” and “sight”?
openers.prompt_hi: School assembly ki poem mein pehli do lines 'light' aur 'bright' par khatam hoti hain. AABB rhyme pattern ke liye agli do lines 'day' aur 'play' par khatam honi chahiye, ya 'night' aur 'sight' par?
hints: In AABB, which lines must rhyme with each other?
The second pair needs a new ending sound.
The next pair is ___ and ___.
Day and play: they rhyme with each other, forming the new pair.

openers.prompt_en: Before a quiz, Meera tells the top scorer, “Only a genius like you can help me. Show me your answers.” Is she offering honest praise or using flattery to get something?
openers.prompt_hi: Quiz se pehle Meera top scorer se kehti hai, 'Sirf tum jaisa genius meri help kar sakta hai. Apne answers dikhao.' Kya yeh honest praise hai ya kuch paane ke liye flattery?
hints: What does Meera want immediately after praising the scorer?
Notice whether the praise serves a request.
Meera's words are ___ because she wants answers.
Flattery: she praises the scorer to get their answers.

harder.prompt_en: A student says, “Captain, nobody solves maths problems as brilliantly as you. Please do my homework.” Why does the student call their classmate “Captain” and praise them?
harder.prompt_hi: Ek student kehta hai, 'Captain, tumse achchha maths koi solve nahi karta. Please mera homework kar do.' Woh classmate ko 'Captain' kehkar uski tareef kyun karta hai?
harder.answer: to make the classmate feel important and persuade them to do the homework
acceptable: to flatter them into doing the homework
so they will do the homework
hints: What favour follows the compliment?
Think about how a grand title might affect the listener.
The student hopes the compliment will make the classmate ___.
To persuade them to do the homework by making them feel important.

verified.solverAnswer: Buttering up to get homework done.

harder.prompt_en: A news report says, “The rescue team sought a safe route through the flooded streets.” Which word from the poem has the same meaning as “sought” here?
harder.prompt_hi: News report mein hai, 'The rescue team sought a safe route through the flooded streets.' Poem ka kaunsa word yahan 'sought' ke meaning se match karta hai?
hints: What was the team trying to find?
Look for a poem word meaning ‘look for’.
The present-tense form of ‘sought’ is ___.
Seek: ‘sought’ means ‘looked for’ and is its past tense.

verified.note: Solver repeated word; key gives synonym

harder.prompt_en: Riya said, “I lost my library card.” Complete the report: Riya said that ___ had lost ___ library card.
harder.prompt_hi: Riya ne kaha, 'I lost my library card.' Reported speech poori karo: Riya said that ___ had lost ___ library card.
acceptable: she had lost her library card
hints: Who does ‘I’ refer to in Riya's words?
Change both the speaker word and the ownership word.
Riya said that ___ had lost ___ library card.
She; her: both words refer to Riya, the speaker and card owner.

openers.prompt_en: At a school event, the lights went out. Meera found a torch, switched it on, then guided her team outside. Which happened immediately before she guided them outside: finding the torch or switching it on?
openers.prompt_hi: School event mein lights chali gayin. Meera ko torch mili, usne torch on ki, phir team ko bahar le gayi. Team ko bahar le jaane se bilkul pehle kya hua: torch milna ya use on karna?
hints: Which action comes directly before guiding the team?
Follow the order of actions, not just the first event.
Found it → ___ → guided the team.
She switched it on; that happened just before she guided them.

openers.prompt_en: A student sees rain approaching during an outdoor match and says, 'Let's check the equipment room.' Her teammate knows their bags are there. Is she more likely worried about the bags or looking for a bat?
openers.prompt_hi: Outdoor match ke dauraan baarish aati dekh ek student kehti hai, ‘Chalo equipment room check karein.’ Uske teammate ko pata hai ki unke bags wahin hain. Use zyada fikr kiski hogi: bags ki ya bat dhoondhne ki?
hints: What might the approaching rain damage?
Connect the weather with what is stored in that room.
She suggests checking the room because their ___ are there.
She is worried about the bags; rain might wet them.

verified.note: Context implies concern for bags, not bat

harder.prompt_en: A shopkeeper notices someone taking items without paying. She calmly says to her assistant, 'Could you ask the guard to check the back door?' Why might she avoid accusing the person aloud?
harder.prompt_hi: Ek shopkeeper dekhti hai ki koi bina paise diye samaan le raha hai. Woh assistant se shaanti se kehti hai, ‘Guard se back door check karne ko kahoge?’ Woh us vyakti par zor se ilzaam kyun nahi lagati?
harder.answer: To get help without alarming the person
acceptable: to call the guard without alerting the person
taaki us vyakti ko satark kiye bina madad mil jaaye
hints: Who does she want her assistant to contact?
Think about how the person might react to an accusation.
She speaks calmly so the person does not ___ before help arrives.
She wants help without alarming the person, who might otherwise flee.

verified.solverAnswer: To avoid causing panic or conflict in public.
verified.note: Both convey discreet help without alarm

harder.prompt_en: On a metro platform, Arjun sees smoke near a bin. Instead of pushing through the crowd, he tells a station worker and moves away. What helped him respond safely: presence of mind or physical strength?
harder.prompt_hi: Metro platform par Arjun ko bin ke paas dhuan dikhta hai. Bheed mein dhakka dene ke bajay woh station worker ko batata hai aur door hat jaata hai. Surakshit tareeke se kaam karne mein kya kaam aaya: presence of mind ya physical strength?
hints: Did Arjun rely on force or a quick decision?
Notice that he sought help and avoided danger.
His safe response shows calm, quick ___.
Presence of mind helped him seek help and move away safely.

harder.prompt_en: During a school play, the audience is silent. Complete the sentence with the correct verb form and adverb: 'The actor ___ (speak) ___ so everyone can hear.' Choose: 'is speaking loudly' or 'speaks softly'.
harder.prompt_hi: School play mein audience chup hai. Sentence ke liye sahi verb form aur adverb chuno: ‘The actor ___ (speak) ___ so everyone can hear.’ Options: ‘is speaking loudly’ ya ‘speaks softly’.
hints: Is the sentence describing an action happening now?
The verb needs an ongoing form; consider how everyone hears.
The actor ___ ___ so everyone can hear.
‘Is speaking loudly’ fits an ongoing action heard by everyone.

openers.prompt_en: At a school event, Tara lost her entry pass. Kabir helped her search, and a guard later found it. What happened just before the guard found the pass?
openers.prompt_hi: School event mein Tara ka entry pass kho gaya. Kabir ne dhoondhne mein madad ki, aur baad mein guard ko pass mila. Guard ko pass milne se just pehle kya hua?
acceptable: Kabir helped her look for it
Kabir and Tara searched for the pass
hints: Which event comes immediately before the guard’s discovery?
Follow the order of actions in the passage.
First Tara lost it; then Kabir ___; finally the guard found it.
Kabir helped Tara search; his help came before the discovery.

openers.prompt_en: Meera saved a seat for a new classmate who had been eating alone. Did Meera most likely want to include the classmate or avoid her?
openers.prompt_hi: Meera ne ek naye classmate ke liye seat bachayi, jo akele lunch kar rahi thi. Meera use include karna chahti thi ya avoid karna?
hints: What might the saved seat allow the classmate to do?
Use Meera’s action to work out her intention.
Saving a seat suggests Meera wanted the classmate to ___.
Include her; saving a seat invites her to join.

harder.prompt_en: Arjun loves cricket; Zoya prefers chess. They practise together for a quiz. When Zoya gets selected and Arjun does not, he cheers for her. Why does this show that friendship need not depend on being alike?
harder.prompt_hi: Arjun ko cricket pasand hai; Zoya ko chess. Dono quiz ke liye saath practise karte hain. Zoya select hoti hai, Arjun nahi, phir bhi woh uske liye cheer karta hai. Yeh friendship ke baare mein kya dikhata hai?
harder.answer: They have different interests, but Arjun cares about Zoya’s happiness.
acceptable: They are different, yet Arjun is happy for Zoya
Friends can be different and still care for each other
hints: Are their interests the same? How does Arjun react?
Compare their differences with Arjun’s response to Zoya’s success.
Although they like different things, Arjun ___ when Zoya succeeds.
They differ, but Arjun cares about her happiness; friendship needs care, not sameness.

verified.solverAnswer: Friendship is based on care and support, not shared interests.
verified.note: Both explain differing interests yet caring

harder.prompt_en: The school app says, ‘The bus arrival time was ___ because the driver entered the wrong time.’ Add a prefix to ‘reported’ to complete the sentence.
harder.prompt_hi: School app mein likha hai: ‘The bus arrival time was ___ because the driver entered the wrong time.’ ‘Reported’ ke aage prefix lagaakar blank bharo.
hints: Was the time reported correctly?
Choose a prefix that can mean ‘wrongly’.
Prefix + reported = ___ .
Misreported; ‘mis-’ shows the time was reported wrongly.

harder.prompt_en: Complete with the past perfect form of ‘leave’: ‘When Riya reached the metro platform at 8:10, the train ___ at 8:05.’
harder.prompt_hi: ‘Leave’ ka past perfect form lagao: ‘When Riya reached the metro platform at 8:10, the train ___ at 8:05.’
hints: Which action happened earlier?
Use past perfect for the action completed before another past action.
The train ___ before Riya reached the platform.
Had left; the train’s departure happened before Riya arrived.

openers.prompt_en: At a school farewell, Riya reads: “We stand beside each other in the rain / And help each other try again / We cheer when someone learns to grow / And stay together through the snow.” Is the rhyme pattern AABB or ABAB?
openers.prompt_hi: School farewell mein Riya yeh lines padhti hai: “We stand beside each other in the rain / And help each other try again / We cheer when someone learns to grow / And stay together through the snow.” Rhyme pattern AABB hai ya ABAB?
hints: Which lines have matching sounds at the end?
Compare the first pair of endings, then the second pair.
The matching lines are ___ and ___; then ___ and ___.
AABB: each pair of neighbouring lines rhymes.

openers.prompt_en: Before a kabaddi match, Aman says, “I hope I can support my teammate even if she misses a point.” Is his wish mainly to win, to be a good friend, or to change his teammate?
openers.prompt_hi: Kabaddi match se pehle Aman kehta hai, “I hope I can support my teammate even if she misses a point.” Uski wish mainly jeetne ki hai, achha dost banne ki, ya teammate ko badalne ki?
hints: What does Aman hope to do after a mistake?
Notice whose behaviour he wants to guide.
His wish is to be a ___ to his teammate.
To be a good friend: he wants to support her despite a mistake.

harder.prompt_en: A poem’s speaker says, “May I listen before I judge a friend.” Why does this sound like a prayer rather than a description? Answer in a short phrase.
harder.prompt_hi: Ek poem ka speaker kehta hai, “May I listen before I judge a friend.” Yeh description ke bajay prayer kyun lagti hai? Chhote phrase mein batao.
harder.answer: It asks for help to become a better friend.
acceptable: It expresses a wish to be a better friend.
It asks to become more understanding.
hints: Is the speaker reporting something done or hoping for something?
Think about what the speaker wants to change in themselves.
It sounds like a prayer because the speaker asks to ___.
It asks for help to become a better friend, rather than describing an action.

verified.solverAnswer: it asks for a quality rather than stating a fact
verified.note: Both convey seeking help to improve

harder.prompt_en: Meera keeps her teammate’s confidence and supports her after a poor cricket innings. Which word best fits Meera: loyal, blessed, or honest?
harder.prompt_hi: Meera apni teammate ki private baat kisi ko nahi batati aur kharab cricket innings ke baad bhi uska saath deti hai. Meera ke liye kaunsa word best hai: loyal, blessed, ya honest?
hints: Does Meera stand by her teammate?
Choose the word about staying supportive through difficulty.
A friend who stands by someone is ___.
Loyal: Meera stands by her teammate after a difficult innings.

harder.prompt_en: For a friend travelling to a chess tournament, choose the correct wish: “May you reach safely” or “May you reaches safely”?
harder.prompt_hi: Chess tournament ke liye travel kar rahe dost ko wish karni hai. Kaunsa sahi hai: “May you reach safely” ya “May you reaches safely”?
hints: Which verb form follows ‘May you’?
After ‘may’, use the plain form of the verb.
May you ___ safely.
May you reach safely: ‘may’ takes the plain verb ‘reach’.

openers.prompt_en: At a school fair, Riya bet she could balance a tray without help. The tray tilted, her friends steadied it, and she shared the snacks with them. What happened immediately before Riya shared the snacks?
openers.prompt_hi: School fair mein Riya ne bet lagayi ki woh tray bina help ke balance karegi. Tray jhuki, friends ne use sambhala, aur Riya ne snacks share kiye. Snacks share karne se turant pehle kya hua?
hints: Which event comes just before the snacks?
Follow the events in the order given.
The tray tilted; then her friends ___ it.
Her friends steadied the tray; that happened before the snacks were shared.

openers.prompt_en: Before a cricket match, Kabir announced he would hit every ball for six. When he missed the first ball, he asked his team for advice. At first, was Kabir modest or boastful?
openers.prompt_hi: Cricket match se pehle Kabir ne kaha ki woh har ball par six marega. Pehli ball miss hui toh usne team se advice maangi. Shuru mein Kabir modest tha ya boastful?
hints: What did Kabir claim before the match?
Judge his attitude from that claim, not his later request.
Claiming you will hit every ball for six sounds ___.
Boastful; he made an exaggerated claim about his batting.

harder.prompt_en: When Sana dropped her project, some classmates laughed. Meera helped collect the pieces and stayed to rebuild it. Why is Meera a truer friend than the classmates who laughed? Answer in one short phrase.
harder.prompt_hi: Sana ka project gir gaya toh kuch classmates hanse. Meera ne pieces uthaye aur project dobara banane mein saath diya. Meera un classmates se zyada sachchi dost kyun hai? Ek short phrase mein batao.
harder.answer: She helped Sana when things went wrong.
acceptable: Mushkil mein Sana ki madad ki
hints: What did each person do after the project fell?
Compare their actions when Sana needed support.
Meera showed friendship by ___ Sana.
She helped Sana when things went wrong; the others only laughed.

harder.prompt_en: Complete this sentence with the correct form of ‘carry’: ‘Aarav was ___ the team’s water bottles when the match ended.’
harder.prompt_hi: ‘Carry’ ka sahi form lagakar sentence complete karo: ‘Aarav was ___ the team’s water bottles when the match ended.’
hints: What verb form follows ‘was’ here?
Add the action suffix; check what happens to final y.
carry + ing = ___.
Carrying; ‘was’ takes the -ing form, and the y stays.

harder.prompt_en: Combine these into one sentence using ‘who’: ‘The volunteer found my lost metro card. She handed it to the station officer.’
harder.prompt_hi: ‘Who’ use karke inhe ek sentence banao: ‘The volunteer found my lost metro card. She handed it to the station officer.’
harder.answer: The volunteer who found my lost metro card handed it to the station officer.
acceptable: The volunteer who found my lost metro card gave it to the station officer
hints: Which person do both sentences describe?
Put the identifying detail directly after that person.
The volunteer who ___ handed it to the station officer.
The volunteer who found my lost metro card handed it to the station officer.

verified.solverAnswer: The volunteer who found my lost metro card handed it to the station officer.

openers.prompt_en: At a school exhibition, Riya asks, “Why are neem leaves kept with these stored clothes?” The guide replies, “They help keep insects away.” What use of neem leaves should Riya note?
openers.prompt_hi: School exhibition mein Riya poochti hai, “In rakhe hue kapdon ke saath neem ke patte kyun hain?” Guide kehta hai, “Ye keedon ko door rakhne mein madad karte hain.” Riya neem ke patton ka kaunsa upyog likhe?
openers.answer: They help keep insects away from stored clothes.
hints: What was Riya trying to find out?
Connect the guide’s reply to the clothes on display.
Neem leaves help protect stored clothes from ____.
They keep insects away from stored clothes; that is the guide’s point.

verified.note: Solver too vague on specific use

openers.prompt_en: A gardening club note says: “Neem twigs can be used to clean teeth; neem oil is used to make soap.” In a ‘tree part → use’ table, what should go beside ‘neem oil’?
openers.prompt_hi: Gardening club ke note mein likha hai: “Neem ki datun se daant saaf kiye ja sakte hain; neem ka tel sabun banane mein istemal hota hai.” ‘Tree part → use’ table mein ‘neem oil’ ke saamne kya likhoge?
hints: Which part is named in the table row?
Match that part to its use in the note.
Neem oil → used to make ____.
Used to make soap; the note links oil with soap.

harder.prompt_en: In a school play, an old neem tree says, “Sit in my shade, and I’ll tell you what my leaves can do.” Why does the writer let the tree speak: to share its uses engagingly, or to give a scientific report?
harder.prompt_hi: School play mein ek purana neem ka ped kehta hai, “Meri chhaon mein baitho; main bataunga mere patte kya kar sakte hain.” Writer ped ko kyun bolne deta hai: uske upyog dilchasp tareeke se batane ke liye, ya scientific report dene ke liye?
acceptable: to tell us about its uses in an engaging way
upyog dilchasp tareeke se batane ke liye
hints: Can a real tree speak to an audience?
Think about how a speaking character affects listeners.
The writer makes the tree speak to make its uses ____.
To share its uses engagingly; a speaking tree holds listeners’ interest.

harder.prompt_en: A school poster calls a neem-based project ‘cost-effective’. Is ‘cost-effective’ an open, closed, or hyphenated compound word? Give the category only.
harder.prompt_hi: School poster neem par bane project ko ‘cost-effective’ kehta hai. ‘Cost-effective’ open, closed ya hyphenated compound word hai? Sirf category batao.
hints: How are the two parts joined?
Look for a mark between the words.
Words joined by that mark are called ____ compounds.
Hyphenated; a hyphen joins ‘cost’ and ‘effective’.

harder.prompt_en: Complete the science-club report with the correct verb forms: “Yesterday, Meera ___ (find) a neem fact sheet and ___ (give) it to her teacher.” Say both words in order.
harder.prompt_hi: Science club ki report mein sahi verb forms bharo: “Yesterday, Meera ___ (find) a neem fact sheet and ___ (give) it to her teacher.” Dono words isi order mein bolo.
hints: When did these actions happen?
Both verbs need their irregular past forms.
Yesterday, Meera ___ a fact sheet and ___ it to her teacher.
Found, gave; both are irregular past forms for yesterday’s actions.

openers.prompt_en: A poem about a metro ride has four lines ending in station, light, window, night. Which rhyme scheme fits: ABCB or AABB?
openers.prompt_hi: Metro ride wali poem ki chaar lines station, light, window, night par khatam hoti hain. Kaunsi rhyme scheme sahi hai: ABCB ya AABB?
hints: Which two ending words have the same final sound?
Give matching letters only to words that rhyme.
The line-ending pattern is A–B–C–__.
ABCB: only light and night rhyme.

openers.prompt_en: A bird first sees only its nest. After flying out, it sees branches and rooftops. Which describes its new idea of the world: only the nest, or larger than the nest?
openers.prompt_hi: Ek bird pehle sirf apna nest dekhti hai. Udne ke baad use branches aur rooftops dikhte hain. Ab uske liye duniya kaisi hai: sirf nest, ya nest se badi?
hints: What could the bird see before it flew?
Compare its first view with everything it sees later.
Its new idea includes the nest and things __ it.
Larger than the nest: it now sees branches and rooftops too.

harder.prompt_en: Meera thought her neighbourhood had every kind of shop. On a trip across Delhi, she discovered many unfamiliar markets. Why might she now say, ‘I still have more to learn’?
harder.prompt_hi: Meera sochti thi ki uske neighbourhood mein har tarah ki shop hai. Delhi ghoomkar use kai naye markets mile. Ab woh ‘Mujhe abhi aur seekhna hai’ kyun kahegi?
harder.answer: Seeing more showed her that her earlier view was limited.
acceptable: Her world was bigger than she had thought.
She realised she did not know everything.
Usse pata chala ki woh sab kuch nahi jaanti thi.
hints: What changed after Meera travelled?
Think about the difference between one neighbourhood and a whole city.
Her earlier idea was limited because __.
Seeing more showed her that her earlier view was limited.

verified.solverAnswer: Her trip showed shops beyond her neighbourhood.
verified.note: Solver gives example, not the reason

harder.prompt_en: For a science display, Anaya made a model moon from a grey, round ball of paper. Which phrase describes its colour, shape and material, in that order: ‘grey round paper’ or ‘round grey paper’?
harder.prompt_hi: Science display ke liye Anaya ne paper ki grey, round ball se moon banaya. Colour, shape aur material isi order mein kaunsa phrase batata hai: ‘grey round paper’ ya ‘round grey paper’?
hints: Which detail tells you the colour?
Keep the details in the order the question asks for.
Colour → shape → material: __ → __ → __.
Grey round paper: grey is colour, round is shape, paper is material.

harder.prompt_en: Complete the sentence with the correct past-belief form: ‘I ___ (believe) all trains stopped at my station, but now I know some pass through.’
harder.prompt_hi: Past belief batane ke liye sentence poora karo: ‘I ___ (believe) all trains stopped at my station, but now I know some pass through.’
hints: Does the speaker still hold this belief?
Use the form for something true in the past but not now.
Write ‘used to’ followed by the plain verb: used to __.
Used to believe: it contrasts an old belief with what the speaker knows now.

ongrade.prompt_en: A poem about a bird has four lines ending in sky, ground, high, sound. Write the rhyme scheme, giving the same letter to words that rhyme.
ongrade.prompt_hi: Ek bird wali poem ki chaar lines sky, ground, high, sound par khatam hoti hain. Rhyming words ko same letter dekar rhyme scheme likho.
hints: Which line endings sound alike?
Give the first ending A; give a different sound B.
sky = A, ground = B, high = ___, sound = ___.
ABAB: sky rhymes with high, and ground with sound.

ongrade.prompt_en: A bird in a nest says, “The world ends at these branches.” Later, it flies over a lake and fields. What does its new view show about its earlier belief: it was complete or limited?
ongrade.prompt_hi: Nest mein bird kehta hai, ‘Duniya in branches tak hi hai.’ Baad mein woh lake aur fields ke upar udta hai. Naya nazara dikhata hai ki uska pehle ka belief complete tha ya limited?
hints: What could the bird see before it flew?
Compare the first view with what it sees later.
Its earlier belief was ___ because it had seen less.
Limited: flying showed the bird places beyond the branches.

ongrade.prompt_en: Complete the sentence about a changed belief: “Before I travelled by train, I ___ (think) all stations were equally busy. Now I know they are not.” Use “used to” and the verb given.
ongrade.prompt_hi: Badle hue belief wali sentence complete karo: ‘Before I travelled by train, I ___ (think) all stations were equally busy. Now I know they are not.’ ‘Used to’ aur diya hua verb use karo.
hints: Is the speaker describing an old belief or a present one?
After ‘used to’, use the plain form of the verb.
I used to ___ all stations were equally busy.
Used to think: it describes a belief held in the past.

openers.prompt_en: In a letter to her cousin, Meera writes, “I’m sharing our family’s kitchen tips. Ajwain is often used for stomach discomfort, while ginger is used for a cough.” Which spice does Meera connect with stomach discomfort?
openers.prompt_hi: Apne cousin ko letter mein Meera likhti hai, “Main family ke kitchen tips share kar rahi hoon. Ajwain pet ki takleef ke liye aur ginger khaansi ke liye use hota hai.” Pet ki takleef se woh kaunsa spice jodti hai?
hints: Letter mein stomach discomfort waali baat dhoondho.
Har spice ko uske saath likhi takleef se jodo.
Stomach discomfort → ___.
Ajwain; letter mein use stomach discomfort se joda gaya hai.

openers.prompt_en: A school food-fair label names the spice “heeng” in Hindi. What English spice name should go beside it?
openers.prompt_hi: School food fair ke label par spice ka Hindi naam “heeng” likha hai. Uske saath English mein kaunsa spice name likhenge?
hints: Is Hindi spice ka English naam yaad karo.
Spice-name list mein iski matching entry dhoondho.
Heeng → ___.
Asafoetida; yeh heeng ka English naam hai.

harder.prompt_en: A grandmother writes, “My mother taught me to use clove for toothache. Ask an elder before trying it, and visit a dentist if the pain continues.” Why does she mention the dentist?
harder.prompt_hi: Daadi likhti hain, “Meri maa ne mujhe toothache mein laung use karna sikhaya. Use karne se pehle elder se poochho, aur dard bana rahe toh dentist ko dikhao.” Woh dentist ka zikr kyun karti hain?
harder.answer: Clove is not a substitute for dental treatment if the pain continues.
acceptable: A continuing toothache needs a dentist
The remedy may give relief but cannot replace a dentist
hints: Pain continues toh letter kya karne ko kehta hai?
Gharelu nuskhe aur professional treatment ka farq socho.
The remedy does not replace ___.
Clove cannot replace dental treatment when pain continues.

verified.solverAnswer: For professional care if the pain continues.
verified.note: Both stress need for dentist if pain persists

harder.prompt_en: Correct this advice from a school wellness poster: “You should to ask an elder before trying a home remedy.” Say the corrected sentence.
harder.prompt_hi: School wellness poster ki advice theek karo: “You should to ask an elder before trying a home remedy.” Corrected sentence bolo.
harder.answer: You should ask an elder before trying a home remedy.
acceptable: You should ask an elder before trying a home remedy
hints: Should ke baad verb ka kaunsa form aata hai?
Modal ke baad plain verb lagta hai.
You should ___ an elder before trying a home remedy.
You should ask an elder before trying a home remedy; ‘should’ takes the plain verb.

verified.solverAnswer: You should ask an elder before trying a home remedy.

harder.prompt_en: For a school cooking demo, complete both questions with “much” or “many”: “How ___ ginger do we need? How ___ cloves do we need?” Give the words in order.
harder.prompt_hi: School cooking demo ke liye dono questions mein “much” ya “many” bharo: “How ___ ginger do we need? How ___ cloves do we need?” Words order mein batao.
acceptable: much for ginger, many for cloves
hints: In dono ingredients mein kise alag-alag gin sakte ho?
Uncountable aur countable nouns ke liye alag quantity words lagte hain.
How ___ ginger? How ___ cloves?
Much, many; ginger uncountable hai, cloves gine ja sakte hain.

openers.prompt_en: Before a chess match, Aman feared losing. He secretly moved a piece, won, but felt uneasy. Later, he played fairly and enjoyed himself. Which feeling came immediately after his dishonest win: fear, unease, or enjoyment?
openers.prompt_hi: Chess match se pehle Aman haarne se darta tha. Usne chupke se ek piece hilaya aur jeet gaya, par use achha nahi laga. Baad mein fair khelkar usne maza liya. Beimaani wali jeet ke turant baad kya mehsoos hua: dar, bechaini, ya maza?
hints: Which event happened just before the feeling you need?
Follow the order of actions and feelings.
Dishonest win → ___ → fair play.
Unease; the dishonest win made Aman feel uneasy.

openers.prompt_en: Riya hated losing at kabaddi. She watched a teammate congratulate the winners and eagerly join another match. Soon Riya did the same. What changed Riya's attitude: watching her teammate, practising raids, or counting points?
openers.prompt_hi: Riya ko kabaddi mein haarna bilkul pasand nahi tha. Usne apni teammate ko winners ko badhai dete aur agla match khushi se khelte dekha. Phir Riya ne bhi aisa kiya. Uski soch kis se badli: teammate ko dekhkar, raids practice karke, ya points ginkar?
hints: What did Riya notice before she changed?
Look for a behaviour she could copy.
She changed after ___ her teammate.
Watching her teammate; Riya copied her positive response to losing.

harder.prompt_en: In a school quiz, Dev secretly checks an answer on his phone and wins. Meera loses but asks to join the next quiz. Who shows sporting spirit, Dev or Meera? Why? Answer in one short phrase.
harder.prompt_hi: School quiz mein Dev chupke se phone par answer dekhkar jeet jaata hai. Meera haarti hai, phir bhi agle quiz mein hissa lena chahti hai. Sporting spirit kaun dikhata hai, Dev ya Meera? Ek chhote phrase mein wajah batao.
harder.answer: Meera, because she enjoys taking part even after losing
acceptable: Meera; she wants to play again despite losing
Meera, kyunki haarne ke baad bhi woh khelna chahti hai
hints: Who wants to take part again?
Sporting spirit values fair participation beyond the result.
___ shows it because losing does not stop her from ___.
Meera; she wants to participate again despite losing.

verified.solverAnswer: Meera, because she accepts loss and tries again.

harder.prompt_en: At the cricket final, the scoreboard showed 84 runs for each team. The scorer checked her tally before announcing a tie. In this sentence, does “tally” mean a record of scores or a practice session?
harder.prompt_hi: Cricket final mein scoreboard par dono teams ke 84 runs the. Tie announce karne se pehle scorer ne apni tally check ki. Is sentence mein “tally” ka matlab scores ka record hai ya practice session?
hints: What would a scorer check before announcing a result?
Use the scoreboard and the scorer as clues.
Here, tally means a ___ used to check the result.
A record of scores; the scorer checks it before announcing a tie.

harder.prompt_en: Complete both blanks: “By the time the metro arrived, Nisha ___ already ___ her ticket. She ___ board because it was valid.” Use the past perfect of “buy” and the correct form of “could”.
harder.prompt_hi: Dono blanks bharo: “By the time the metro arrived, Nisha ___ already ___ her ticket. She ___ board because it was valid.” “Buy” ka past perfect aur “could” ka sahi form use karo.
hints: Which action happened before the metro arrived?
Use had plus the third form for the earlier action.
Nisha ___ already ___ her ticket; she ___ board.
Had bought; could. Buying came first, and the valid ticket allowed boarding.

openers.prompt_en: A poem about a kabaddi match ends with these lines: 'I / stop / and / breathe.' Why might the poet put one word on each line: to show breathless pauses or to make a regular rhyme?
openers.prompt_hi: Kabaddi match par poem ki last lines hain: 'I / stop / and / breathe.' Poet har line mein ek word kyun likhta hai: saans ke liye rukna dikhane ko, ya regular rhyme banane ko?
acceptable: the player is out of breath
hints: How would you read the gaps between these lines?
Think about the player's breathing after a match.
The short lines make the reader pause as if ___ .
They show breathless pauses, like a tired player stopping for air.

openers.prompt_en: Read: 'At sunset, Meera and Dev practised badminton in the park. When the lights went out, they could no longer see the shuttlecock.' What changed that made them stop playing?
openers.prompt_hi: Padho: 'At sunset, Meera and Dev practised badminton in the park. When the lights went out, they could no longer see the shuttlecock.' Kya badla jiski wajah se unhein khelna rokna pada?
hints: What happened just before they lost sight of the shuttlecock?
Look for the change in the second sentence.
They stopped because ___ .
The lights went out, so they could not see the shuttlecock.

verified.solverAnswer: They could no longer see the shuttlecock.

harder.prompt_en: Read: 'We raced until dusk. The shadows swallowed our playground, and even the fastest runner went home.' Why does the speaker say the shadows won?
harder.prompt_hi: Padho: 'We raced until dusk. The shadows swallowed our playground, and even the fastest runner went home.' Speaker kyun kehta hai ki shadows jeet gayi?
harder.answer: Darkness ended the game, not a runner
acceptable: it got too dark to race
andhere ki wajah se game khatam hua
hints: Did a runner finish first in this account?
Think about what made everyone leave.
The shadows 'won' because ___ .
Darkness ended the game; no runner's speed decided it.

harder.prompt_en: For the school nature walk, a guide describes a narrow flow of water moving between rocks. Which word fits best: creek, pond, or lake?
harder.prompt_hi: School nature walk mein guide batata hai: rocks ke beech se paani ki ek patli dhaara beh rahi hai. Kaunsa word best hai: creek, pond, ya lake?
hints: Is this water still or moving?
Compare the size and movement of the three options.
A narrow moving flow is a ___ .
Creek fits: it is a small, flowing water body.

harder.prompt_en: Aarav plays cricket every Sunday. Complete his sentence about the usual result: 'I hit the ball so far ___ my friends have to run to the boundary.'
harder.prompt_hi: Aarav har Sunday cricket khelta hai. Uske usual result waale sentence ko complete karo: 'I hit the ball so far ___ my friends have to run to the boundary.'
acceptable: that my friends have to run to the boundary
hints: Which word connects the distance to its result?
Recall the two-part pattern for degree and result.
I hit the ball so far ___ my friends have to run.
That completes 'so far that', linking the hit to its result.

openers.prompt_en: A school notice says, “Yoga includes movement and careful breathing. Both can help students feel calmer.” Which is its main idea: A) yoga can support well-being, or B) students need a school notice?
openers.prompt_hi: School notice mein likha hai, “Yoga mein movement aur dhyaan se saans lena shamil hai. Dono students ko shaant mehsoos karne mein madad kar sakte hain.” Main idea kya hai: A) yoga well-being mein madad kar sakta hai, ya B) students ko school notice chahiye?
hints: Which option covers both movement and careful breathing?
A main idea brings the supporting details together.
The details about feeling calmer support option ___.
A: yoga can support well-being; feeling calmer supports that idea.

openers.prompt_en: After weeks of yoga, Meera could bend more easily to tie her running shoes. Which word best describes this change: flexibility, distraction, or anxiety?
openers.prompt_hi: Kai hafton ke yoga ke baad Meera apne running shoes baandhne ke liye zyada aasani se jhuk paayi. Is badlav ke liye kaunsa word sahi hai: flexibility, distraction, ya anxiety?
hints: What physical change does bending more easily show?
Match the word to easier movement, not a feeling.
Bending more easily shows improved ___.
Flexibility: it means being able to bend and move more easily.

harder.prompt_en: During a yoga posture, Kabir keeps thinking about tomorrow’s cricket match and loses his balance. Why should he bring his attention back to his body? Answer in one short phrase.
harder.prompt_hi: Yoga posture karte waqt Kabir kal ke cricket match ke baare mein sochta rehta hai aur balance kho deta hai. Use apna dhyaan body par wapas kyun lana chahiye? Ek chhote phrase mein batao.
harder.answer: To keep his mind and body working together
acceptable: to keep his mind with his body
hints: What changed just before Kabir lost his balance?
Think about where his attention needs to be during the posture.
He should focus on his body so his mind and body ___.
To keep his mind and body working together; attention supports balance.

verified.note: solver gives outcome, key gives reason

harder.prompt_en: Complete the message: “Our coach gave us useful ___ before the yoga session and will ___ us again tomorrow.” Choose one pair: A) advice, advise; B) advise, advice.
harder.prompt_hi: Message complete karo: “Our coach gave us useful ___ before the yoga session and will ___ us again tomorrow.” Ek pair chuno: A) advice, advise; B) advise, advice.
hints: Which blank names something the coach gave?
The first blank needs a noun; the second needs a verb.
Our coach gave us useful ___ and will ___ us again.
A: advice is the noun; advise is the verb.

harder.prompt_en: Choose the grammatically correct instruction for a class yoga video: A) “First, Rohan breathe slowly; then, he stretch.” B) “First, Rohan breathes slowly; then, he stretches.”
harder.prompt_hi: Class yoga video ke liye grammatically sahi instruction chuno: A) “First, Rohan breathe slowly; then, he stretch.” B) “First, Rohan breathes slowly; then, he stretches.”
harder.answer: B) First, Rohan breathes slowly; then, he stretches.
acceptable: First, Rohan breathes slowly; then, he stretches.
hints: Who performs each action in the sentence?
With one named person, check both present-simple verbs.
First, Rohan ___ slowly; then, he ___.
B: breathes and stretches agree with Rohan and he.

verified.solverAnswer: B) “First, Rohan breathes slowly; then, he stretches.”

openers.prompt_en: At a school fair, Meera sings a Tamil song and Arjun performs a Punjabi dance. Both help organise the same event. What is the main idea: different arts bring students together, or one art is better than the other?
openers.prompt_hi: School fair mein Meera Tamil song gaati hai aur Arjun Punjabi dance karta hai. Dono milkar event organise karte hain. Main idea kya hai: different arts bring students together, ya one art is better than the other?
acceptable: Alag-alag kalaayein students ko saath laati hain.
hints: What do the students do together?
Choose the idea supported by both performances and their shared work.
Their different arts help them ___.
Different arts bring students together; both contribute to one event.

openers.prompt_en: Nisha says, ‘In Gujarat, my aunt makes bandhani scarves by tying and dyeing cloth.’ In a table with columns State, Art form, Material, what belongs under Material?
openers.prompt_hi: Nisha kehti hai, ‘Gujarat mein meri aunt kapde ko baandhkar aur rangkar bandhani scarves banati hain.’ State, Art form, Material waali table mein Material ke neeche kya likhoge?
hints: What does the aunt tie and dye?
Material means the substance used to make something.
The scarf is made from ___.
Cloth; it is the material tied and dyed.

harder.prompt_en: For a school display, Zoya washes a used jar, dries it, paints it, then puts flowers inside. Which step comes immediately after drying: painting or adding flowers?
harder.prompt_hi: School display ke liye Zoya used jar dhoti hai, sukhaati hai, paint karti hai, phir usmein phool rakhti hai. Sukhaane ke turant baad kaunsa step hai: painting ya adding flowers?
hints: Which action follows drying in the description?
Track the actions in their stated order.
Wash, dry, ___, add flowers.
Painting; it comes between drying and adding flowers.

harder.prompt_en: A craft club must choose between leaf plates and plastic-coated plates for an event. If they want plates that can break down naturally, which should they choose?
harder.prompt_hi: Craft club ko event ke liye leaf plates aur plastic-coated plates mein se chunna hai. Agar unhe naturally galne waali plates chahiye, toh kya chunenge?
acceptable: leaf plates because they are biodegradable
hints: Which material can break down naturally?
Think about what biodegradable means.
Choose plates made from ___.
Leaf plates; leaves can break down naturally.

harder.prompt_en: Choose the correctly written sentence: (A) ‘ravi makes Madhubani paintings in Bihar.’ (B) ‘Ravi make Madhubani paintings in bihar.’ (C) ‘Ravi makes Madhubani paintings in Bihar.’
harder.prompt_hi: Sahi likha hua sentence chuno: (A) ‘ravi makes Madhubani paintings in Bihar.’ (B) ‘Ravi make Madhubani paintings in bihar.’ (C) ‘Ravi makes Madhubani paintings in Bihar.’
acceptable: Ravi makes Madhubani paintings in Bihar.
hints: Check the verb and the capital letters.
A single named person takes the matching present-simple verb form.
The correct sentence has ___ capitals and verb form.
C; ‘Ravi’ and ‘Bihar’ are capitalised, and ‘makes’ agrees.

ongrade.prompt_en: At a school exhibition, students display Assamese weaving, Kashmiri embroidery and Tamil folk paintings. Each explains the art to visitors from other states. What is the main idea: (A) one art is best, (B) sharing different traditions brings people together, or (C) all crafts use cloth?
ongrade.prompt_hi: School exhibition mein students Assamese weaving, Kashmiri embroidery aur Tamil folk paintings dikhate hain. Har student doosre states ke visitors ko apni art samjhata hai. Main idea kya hai: (A) ek art sabse achchhi hai, (B) alag traditions share karne se log judte hain, ya (C) sab crafts mein kapda lagta hai?
ongrade.answer: B — sharing different traditions brings people together
acceptable: sharing different traditions brings people together
alag traditions share karne se log judte hain
hints: What connects all three displays?
Look beyond the art forms to what the students do together.
The passage is mainly about sharing different traditions to ___.
B: Sharing traditions helps people from different states connect.

ongrade.prompt_en: For a school craft table, Farah describes making papier-mâché masks in Kashmir: she shapes wet paper pulp over a mould, lets it dry, and paints it. What should go in the ‘material’ column for Farah’s craft?
ongrade.prompt_hi: School craft table ke liye Farah batati hai ki Kashmir mein papier-mâché masks kaise bante hain: woh geele paper pulp ko mould par shape deti hai, sukhati hai aur paint karti hai. Farah ke craft ke ‘material’ column mein kya likhoge?
hints: Which substance does Farah shape?
Separate the material from the mould and the finished mask.
The material column should say ___.
Wet paper pulp: it is shaped over the mould.

ongrade.prompt_en: A craft group makes block prints: (a) press the inked block onto cloth, (b) let the cloth dry, (c) carve a design into a wooden block, (d) apply ink to the block. Give the letters in the correct order.
ongrade.prompt_hi: Craft group block prints banata hai: (a) ink lage block ko kapde par dabao, (b) kapde ko sukhne do, (c) wooden block par design carve karo, (d) block par ink lagao. Letters ka sahi order batao.
hints: Which step prepares the block itself?
The design must exist before ink can be applied.
Carve, ink, ___, dry.
c, d, a, b: carve and ink before printing, then dry.

openers.prompt_en: At a school kite festival, Riya writes: “My kite climbs past the tree / Its paper catches light / I let the long line run free / It dances out of sight.” Which lines rhyme: 1 and 3, or 2 and 4?
openers.prompt_hi: School kite festival ke liye Riya likhti hai: “My kite climbs past the tree / Its paper catches light / I let the long line run free / It dances out of sight.” Kaunsi lines rhyme karti hain: 1 aur 3, ya 2 aur 4?
hints: Har line ke aakhri word ki sound suno.
Rhyming words ki ending sound milti hai.
Pehli pair ___; doosri pair ___.
Both pairs rhyme: tree/free and light/sight.

openers.prompt_en: From her terrace, Ananya watches a kite above the metro station. She says, “If I could ride it, I’d see the trains as tiny silver lines.” Is she describing what she sees now or what she imagines?
openers.prompt_hi: Terrace se Ananya metro station ke upar ek kite dekhti hai. Woh kehti hai, “If I could ride it, I’d see the trains as tiny silver lines.” Kya woh abhi jo dekh rahi hai woh bata rahi hai, ya apni imagination?
hints: Kya Ananya sach mein kite par baithi hai?
‘If I could’ ek sambhavana sochne ka signal hai.
Woh apni ___ bata rahi hai.
She imagines the view; she is still on the terrace.

harder.prompt_en: A festival poster says, “The kites floated like bright fish above Jaipur.” Is “like bright fish” a simile or alliteration? Why?
harder.prompt_hi: Festival poster par likha hai, “The kites floated like bright fish above Jaipur.” “Like bright fish” simile hai ya alliteration? Kyun?
harder.answer: Simile; it compares kites with fish using ‘like’.
acceptable: simile, because it uses like to compare
simile; kites are compared to fish
hints: Yahan kites aur fish ke beech kya relation hai?
Comparison batane wale word par dhyan do.
Yeh ___ hai, kyunki kites ko fish se compare kiya gaya hai.
Simile: ‘like’ compares the kites with bright fish.

verified.solverAnswer: simile, because it uses ‘like’ to compare kites to fish

harder.prompt_en: During a kite contest, the wind stops. The kite moves slowly sideways, then suddenly drops towards the ground. Which two verbs fit in order: drift and dive, or soar and glide?
harder.prompt_hi: Kite contest mein hawa ruk jaati hai. Kite dheere se side mein jaati hai, phir achanak zameen ki taraf girti hai. Sahi order kaun sa hai: drift and dive, ya soar and glide?
hints: Pehli movement ki speed aur direction kya hai?
Doosri movement achanak neeche ki taraf hai.
Pehle kite ___ karti hai, phir ___ karti hai.
Drift and dive: it moves slowly sideways, then drops sharply.

harder.prompt_en: Complete this imagined wish with the correct forms: “I wish I ___ on that kite; I ___ glide gently over the cricket ground.” Choose “were, would” or “am, will”.
harder.prompt_hi: Imagined wish ko sahi forms se complete karo: “I wish I ___ on that kite; I ___ glide gently over the cricket ground.” “were, would” ya “am, will” chuno.
acceptable: I wish I were on that kite; I would glide gently over the cricket ground
hints: Kya speaker sach mein kite par hai?
Imagined wish ke liye present fact wali forms nahi chahiye.
I wish I ___; I ___ glide gently.
Were, would: these forms express an imagined wish and action.

openers.prompt_en: A school display has three cards about Ila Sachani: ‘learnt embroidery with her feet’, ‘was born in Amreli’, and ‘showed her work at a state exhibition’. Which card comes first in her life story?
openers.prompt_hi: School display mein Ila Sachani ke teen cards hain: ‘pairon se embroidery seekhi’, ‘Amreli mein janam hua’, aur ‘state exhibition mein kaam dikhaya’. Unki life story mein kaunsa card pehle aayega?
hints: Which event must happen before someone learns a craft?
Arrange the cards by when each event happened, not by importance.
The earliest card is ‘_____’.
‘Was born in Amreli’ comes first; it begins her life story.

openers.prompt_en: For weeks, a craftsperson practised holding a needle with her toes. Her family made time for her to practise, even after early attempts failed. Which value does her continued practice show: determination or impatience?
openers.prompt_hi: Kai hafton tak ek craftsperson ne pair ki ungliyon se sui pakadne ki practice ki. Shuru mein nakaam hone par bhi family ne practice ka time diya. Unki lagataar practice kya dikhati hai: determination ya impatience?
hints: What did she do after the early attempts failed?
Focus on continuing to practise despite difficulty.
Continuing despite failure shows _____.
Determination: she kept practising after unsuccessful attempts.

harder.prompt_en: A school newsletter says, ‘Meera showed great determination while learning embroidery.’ Complete its next sentence with the correct adjective: ‘She was _____ even when the stitches went wrong.’
harder.prompt_hi: School newsletter mein likha hai, ‘Meera showed great determination while learning embroidery.’ Agla sentence sahi adjective se poora karo: ‘She was _____ even when the stitches went wrong.’
hints: What kind of word follows ‘was’ to describe Meera?
Change the noun naming her quality into an adjective.
She was _____ even when the stitches went wrong.
Determined: the adjective describes someone who shows determination.

harder.prompt_en: A craft stall has 18 embroidered bags but only a small amount of thread left. Complete both blanks: ‘There are _____ bags, but there is _____ thread.’ Choose from many, much, a few, and a little.
harder.prompt_hi: Craft stall par 18 embroidered bags hain, lekin dhaaga thoda hi bacha hai. Dono blanks bharo: ‘There are _____ bags, but there is _____ thread.’ many, much, a few, aur a little mein se chuno.
hints: Which item can you count one by one?
Match quantity words to countable bags and uncountable thread.
There are _____ bags, but there is _____ thread.
Many; a little: bags are countable, while only a small amount of thread remains.

harder.prompt_en: At a school craft fair, you want to ask an artist about the place where she learned embroidery. Turn this into a correct interview question: ‘Where you did learn embroidery?’
harder.prompt_hi: School craft fair mein tum artist se poochna chahte ho ki unhone embroidery kahan seekhi. Isse sahi interview question banao: ‘Where you did learn embroidery?’
acceptable: Where did you learn to embroider?
hints: Which word asks about a place?
In this question, put the helping verb before the subject.
Where _____ you learn embroidery?
Where did you learn embroidery? The helping verb comes before ‘you’.

harder.prompt_en: Riya's first embroidery sample was uneven. Her aunt showed her a new stitch, and Riya practised it every evening until her work improved. Which two things helped Riya improve: luck, family support, or determination?
harder.prompt_hi: Riya ki pehli embroidery uneven thi. Uski aunt ne naya stitch sikhaya, aur Riya ne har shaam practice ki. Riya ko behtar hone mein kin do cheezon ne madad ki: luck, family support, ya determination?
acceptable: her aunt's support and regular practice
hints: Who taught Riya, and what did she keep doing?
Look for help from someone else and effort from Riya.
The two choices are ___ and ___.
Family support and determination: her aunt taught her, and she practised regularly.

harder.prompt_en: Complete both blanks: ‘Only ___ volunteers could attend the craft workshop, so the organiser had ___ time to teach each person.’ Choose from: a few, a little, many, much. Use each choice at most once.
harder.prompt_hi: Dono blanks bharo: ‘Only ___ volunteers could attend the craft workshop, so the organiser had ___ time to teach each person.’ Choices hain: a few, a little, many, much. Har choice zyada se zyada ek baar use karo.
acceptable: a few volunteers; a little time
hints: Can you count volunteers? Can you count time here?
Match each quantity phrase to a countable or uncountable noun.
Only ___ volunteers; the organiser had ___ time.
A few; a little: volunteers are countable, but time is uncountable.

harder.prompt_en: At a craft exhibition, turn this statement into a question asking for the method: ‘The artist learned embroidery by watching her grandmother.’ Begin with ‘How’ and keep the tense the same.
harder.prompt_hi: Craft exhibition mein is statement ko method poochhne wale question mein badlo: ‘The artist learned embroidery by watching her grandmother.’ ‘How’ se shuru karo aur tense wahi rakho.
harder.answer: How did the artist learn embroidery?
acceptable: How did the artist learn to embroider?
hints: Which part of the statement tells you the method?
A past-tense question needs a helping verb before the subject.
How ___ the artist ___ embroidery?
How did the artist learn embroidery? ‘Did’ carries the past tense.

verified.solverAnswer: How did the artist learn embroidery?

openers.prompt_en: At a school remembrance event, a student writes: ‘We stand beside the gate; / We pause and quietly wait.’ Which two words form the rhyming couplet?
openers.prompt_hi: School remembrance event ke liye student ne likha: ‘We stand beside the gate; / We pause and quietly wait.’ In do lines ke aakhir mein kaun-se words rhyme karte hain?
hints: Which words come at the ends of the two lines?
A rhyming couplet has matching sounds at the ends of two lines.
The end words are ___ and ___.
Gate and wait rhyme because their ending sounds match.

openers.prompt_en: A school notice says, ‘At the remembrance assembly, we will speak the names of soldiers who died protecting the country and thank them for their service.’ What is the notice’s main purpose: celebration, remembrance or recruitment?
openers.prompt_hi: School notice kehta hai: ‘Remembrance assembly mein hum desh ki raksha karte hue jaan dene wale soldiers ke naam lenge aur unhe dhanyavaad denge.’ Notice ka main purpose kya hai: celebration, remembrance ya recruitment?
hints: What will students do with the soldiers’ names?
Look for the purpose behind speaking their names and giving thanks.
The notice asks students to ___ the soldiers.
Remembrance: the assembly keeps the soldiers’ memory alive.

harder.prompt_en: A poem says, ‘On the wall, their names remain; beside it, a flame burns through the night.’ Why pair the names with the flame?
harder.prompt_hi: Ek poem kehti hai: ‘Deewar par unke naam bane hain; paas mein ek flame raat bhar jalti hai.’ Naam aur flame ko saath dikhane se kya idea milta hai?
acceptable: we keep remembering and honouring the soldiers
soldiers ko hamesha yaad aur honour kiya jaata hai
hints: What stays visible even after night falls?
Think about what lasting names and a continuing flame suggest together.
Together, these images suggest that the soldiers are ___.
The soldiers are remembered continuously; both images suggest lasting memory.

verified.solverAnswer: The flame symbolises their enduring memory and spirit.

harder.prompt_en: For a school tribute, complete the sentence using the noun form of ‘brave’: ‘The rescue team’s ___ gave others hope.’
harder.prompt_hi: School tribute ke liye ‘brave’ ka noun form lagakar sentence complete karo: ‘The rescue team’s ___ gave others hope.’
hints: Does the blank need a describing word or a naming word?
The possessive ‘team’s’ can be followed by a noun naming a quality.
The noun form of ‘brave’ is ___.
Bravery fits: it names the team’s quality.

harder.prompt_en: Your class is preparing a respectful tribute for soldiers. Which suggestion is grammatically correct: ‘Let’s to observe a minute’s silence’ or ‘Let’s observe a minute’s silence’?
harder.prompt_hi: Tumhari class soldiers ke liye respectful tribute taiyaar kar rahi hai. Kaunsa suggestion grammatically correct hai: ‘Let’s to observe a minute’s silence’ ya ‘Let’s observe a minute’s silence’?
hints: What form of the verb follows ‘Let’s’?
A suggestion with ‘Let’s’ uses the plain verb directly.
The correct pattern is ‘Let’s ___ a minute’s silence.’
‘Let’s observe a minute’s silence’ is correct; no ‘to’ follows ‘Let’s’.

harder.prompt_en: At the memorial, Meera reads: ‘Their names are etched in stone, though their voices are gone.’ Why might the writer mention stone rather than paper? Answer in a short phrase.
harder.prompt_hi: Memorial par Meera padhti hai: ‘Their names are etched in stone, though their voices are gone.’ Writer ne paper ke bajay stone kyun kaha hoga? Chhote phrase mein batao.
harder.answer: Because stone lasts, helping their names be remembered for a long time
acceptable: stone lasts longer, so their names are remembered
to show that their memory will last
hints: What happens to paper over many years?
Think about what the material suggests about memory.
Stone suggests their names will remain _____.
Their names will be remembered for a long time because stone lasts.

harder.prompt_en: For a school report, choose the better word: ‘The students laid flowers at the memorial to pay ___ to the soldiers.’ Should the blank be ‘homage’ or ‘courage’?
harder.prompt_hi: School report ke liye sahi word chuno: ‘The students laid flowers at the memorial to pay ___ to the soldiers.’ Blank mein ‘homage’ aayega ya ‘courage’?
hints: What are the flowers meant to express?
Notice which word goes with ‘pay’ when showing respect.
The phrase is ‘pay _____ to the soldiers’.
Homage: ‘pay homage’ means to show respect.

harder.prompt_en: Your class is making a notice for a visit to the National War Memorial. Which line suits a formal notice: ‘All students must report at 8 a.m.’ or ‘Hey everyone, show up at eight!’?
harder.prompt_hi: Tumhari class National War Memorial visit ke liye notice bana rahi hai. Formal notice mein kaunsi line theek hai: ‘All students must report at 8 a.m.’ ya ‘Hey everyone, show up at eight!’?
harder.answer: All students must report at 8 a.m.
acceptable: All students must report at 8 am
hints: Who will read this school notice?
A notice uses clear, formal language rather than chatty words.
Choose the line that states the time without _____.
‘All students must report at 8 a.m.’ is clear and formal.

verified.solverAnswer: All students must report at 8 a.m.
